name: Pressure Track
tagline: Understand your blood pressure, one reading at a time
about: Pressure Track turns home blood-pressure readings into clear averages and trends, checks your measuring technique, decodes sodium on labels and builds DASH-style meal plans.
persona: You are a hypertension nurse specialist: precise about technique and numbers, reassuring, and clear that medication decisions belong to the prescriber.

onboarding.title: Take the guesswork out of your readings
onboarding.subtitle: Tell us your situation so the numbers make sense.

tools.title: Analyse my readings
tools.subtitle: Paste a week or a month
tools.prompt: Analyse: {readings}. Table (Period | Avg systolic | Avg diastolic | Avg pulse | Readings count), up to 3 bullets describing morning-versus-evening and weekday patterns with the evidence, a kv comparing the overall average to the profile target and to general home-monitoring thresholds, and a callout stating which individual readings, if any, are high enough to warrant contacting a clinician today.

tools.title: Am I measuring right?
tools.subtitle: Fix the common mistakes

inputs.label: How you usually measure
inputs.placeholder: sitting on the sofa, after coffee, over a shirt sleeve

tools.prompt: Review the technique '{how}' with a {cuff} cuff. Produce a checklist of correct home-measurement steps in order (5-minute rest, back supported, feet flat, arm at heart level, bare arm, no talking, two readings a minute apart), a table (Mistake spotted | Typical effect on the reading | Fix), and a callout on validated-device lists and cuff sizing.

tools.title: Sodium label check
tools.subtitle: Photo → salt verdict
tools.prompt: Read the nutrition label in the photo. kv (sodium per serving in mg, sodium per 100 g, salt equivalent in g, servings per pack, share of a 1,500 mg day), a text verdict on whether this fits a low-sodium day and how often, and bullets of 3 lower-sodium alternatives in the same food category.

tools.title: DASH-style meal plan
tools.subtitle: 3 days, under 1,500 mg sodium
tools.prompt: Build a 3-day DASH-style plan for '{diet}' with notes '{dislikes}', each day under 1,500 mg sodium. Table (Day | Breakfast | Lunch | Dinner | Snack | Est. sodium mg), a checklist shopping list grouped by aisle, 5 bullets on flavouring without salt (acid, herbs, spice blends, umami), and a callout on potassium caution for people with kidney disease or on certain medications.

tools.title: Why was it high today?
tools.subtitle: Work through the likely causes

inputs.label: The last 24 hours
inputs.placeholder: slept 5h, two coffees, takeaway dinner, argument with the landlord

tools.prompt: The reading {reading} followed: {day}. Table (Possible factor | How much it typically shifts BP | Present today?), steps for the next hour (rest, re-measure protocol, what to write down), 3 bullets on which factors are worth changing this week, and a callout with the numbers and symptoms (180/120 or above, chest pain, severe headache, vision change, breathlessness) that mean seek urgent care.

disclaimer: General information, not medical advice. Do not start, stop or change blood-pressure medication without your prescriber. A reading of 180/120 or higher, or any reading with chest pain, breathlessness, severe headache or vision change, is an emergency.
